parts.text:
Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Patients with depressive disorder had decreased vitamin D levels compared with healthy controls.
Sentence: "The patients with DD had elevated TXB levels and decreased vitamin D levels, as compared to healthy controls."
Measured as: depressive disorder (vs healthy controls)
Population: Children and adolescents with depressive disorder and healthy controls
Intervention: Baseline vitamin D level (observational comparison)
Comparator: Healthy controls
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 58
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: In the RCT, vitamin C supplementation did not affect mood, including depression.
Sentence: "The vitamin C supplementation did not affect mood and serum concentrations of BDNF."
Measured as: depression (mood status)
Population: Healthy subjects with inadequate serum vitamin C (<50 μmol/L), n = 46
Intervention: Vitamin C 500 mg twice a day for 4 weeks
Comparator: Placebo
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 260
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

{
  "rationale": "Study B evaluates vitamin C supplementation rather than vitamin D, making it off-question.",
